newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares ease, seen moving sideways.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares ease, seen moving sideways.

text.p: Slovenian shares eased 0.35 percent and traders said the market was expected to track sideways in the next week or two.
"The market is very unpredictable and volatile because currently there is no strong influence that could initiate a general movement up or down," one trader said.
"Due to the unpredictability of the listed shares a lot of money moved into unlisted shares of newly privatised companies where profits are expected once the companies will be listed," she added.
* The seven-share SBI index fell 3.37 percent to 972.51.
* 10 shares fell and seven rose, while six were untraded.
* Turnover rose to 105.3 million tolars from 37.9 million due to a heavy trading in financial consultancy Dadas.

* Dadas had the highest turnover, rising 2.04 percent to 34,420 tolars on volume of 1,780 shares for total turnover of 61.3 million tolars. Traders said the orders had come from only a small number of investors.
* Bank UBK was the leading decliner, falling 39.92 percent to 9,000 on volume of one share.

* Pharmaceutical trader Salus was the biggest gainer, rising 6.85 percent to 14,625 on volume of 960 shares for total turnover of 14 million tolars. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
